# Scope audit of the three-fiber regimes and their remaining cap geometry

This is a coverage audit, not a resolution of three-fiber OC. Throughout
this note the integer coordinate is one-dimensional, the only nonempty
fibers are at -1,0,1, and all three fibers A,K,B are positive d-dimensional
convex bodies with (A+B)/2 subset K. Unless stated otherwise d>=2. Write

    a=|A|/|K|, b=|B|/|K|, m=1+a+b, Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d.

Exchange the endpoints so that 0<a<=b. Scaling all continuous coordinates
normalizes |K|=1 without changing relative masses or the mixed lattice.

## 1. The actual arbitrary-shape small-endpoint result

The source
`candidate 1350a6f7ed8eb7d0`
proves: for each fixed d>=2 there exists rho_d>0 such that a<=rho_d
implies OC for the triple, with no simplex, equal-volume, homothety,
or centroid-location hypothesis. Its full independent root audit is
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

The proof is not merely the earlier simplex-only result. It normalizes
by a maximal inscribed middle simplex, derives two positive simplex
limits from a hypothetical small-endpoint failure sequence, obtains
uniform endpoint cap credits, and translates the true middle centroid
by an amount proportional to the small endpoint volume. Proper section
continuity only multiplies that small displacement; it does not create
an uncontrolled additive approximation error. Every integer tilt and
purely integer boundary cap is handled.

The constant is nonconstructive. No numeric lower bound for rho_d is
proved. We may, and in this note do, replace it by

    min(rho_d,1/8).                                      (1)

This preserves the theorem and makes 0<rho_d<=1/8 an explicit convention.
An example outside this shrunken sufficient regime is not proof that the
largest possible small-endpoint constant is small. Indeed, if the desired
full theorem is true, the small-endpoint implication could hold for all
ratios. That distinction is essential in interpreting the example below.

## 2. Other proved arbitrary-shape volume tests

A fiber of volume at least m/2 supplies OC at its ordinary centroid.
Therefore any hypothetical failure must have

    a<1+b, b<1+a, 1<a+b.                                (2)

With a<=b, this is equivalently a+b>1 and b-a<1.
Whole-body BM also requires

    a^(1/d)+b^(1/d)<=2.                                 (3)

The midpoint-centroid certificate in
`candidate 9dc053aa681e5ef6` gives an actual middle point
with raw depth at least

    Gamma { R+a },    R=[(a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2]^d.

Thus the additional sufficient condition 2R+a-b>=1 is proved for all
shapes. In particular equal endpoint volumes are completely handled.
Any failure must satisfy

    2R+a-b<1.                                          (4)

Consequently a failure cannot have R=1: exact whole-volume BM equality,
together with no heavy fiber, is already handled by this older certificate.
The unproved range has genuine whole-volume midpoint slack R<1.

The small-endpoint result adds the necessary condition

    a>rho_d.                                            (5)

These conclusions concern full positive fibers. The separate interval
results handle d=1 for three consecutive interval fibers; no higher-d
intrinsic degeneracy is being inferred from them.

## 3. Actual critical geometry available at a middle maximum

Let f(y) be the raw mixed depth at (0,y), y in K. The finite-tilt
compactification and projected-active-normal result in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)` shows that
f is continuous, its directional and tilt minima are attained with a
nonzero continuous normal, and an interior middle maximum admits at
most d+1 actual critical continuous normals with a positive dependence.

The middle maximum is indeed interior here. At any boundary point y,
choose a nonzero supporting continuous normal whose captured middle
volume is zero. Vary the integer tilt until the two endpoint captured
volumes agree. If that common value were positive, BM of the two
captured endpoint bodies would put positive volume in the zero-volume
middle cap, a contradiction. Hence a finite through-point ambient cap
has total volume zero and f(y)=0. In contrast the middle centroid has
mixed depth at least Gamma>0. Compactness therefore puts every middle
maximizer in int K.

Fix such a maximum y, and write its raw depth as Q. Its finite actual
critical caps can be written

    H_i={u_i.(x-y)+alpha_i z>=0}, u_i nonzero,
    sum_i theta_i u_i=0, theta_i>0.

Their middle traces cover R^d and hence K. Define their ACTUAL captured
volumes U_i,q_i,V_i. Then

    U_i+q_i+V_i=Q,
    0<=U_i<=a, 0<q_i<1, 0<=V_i<=b,                     (6)
    U_i+V_i<=a,                                        (7)
    Q<=3q_i.                                          (8)

Equation (7) is the two finite saturated-tilt comparison; (8) is the
finite equalization lemma. Both are proved in
`candidate fee4b98d94ecbcf2`.
They do not require proper endpoint cuts.

If both captured endpoint bodies have positive volume, their actual
Minkowski midpoint lies in the middle cap, so

    U_i^(1/d)+V_i^(1/d)<=2q_i^(1/d).                    (9)

No assertion (9) is made from BM when an endpoint cap is empty. If both
strict endpoint residuals are nonempty, the analogous valid inequality is

    (a-U_i)^(1/d)+(b-V_i)^(1/d)<=2(1-q_i)^(1/d).       (10)

This follows by compact strict subcuts and continuity from below. These
conditions cannot be replaced by arbitrary independently allocated
numbers; the same bodies, source, and ambient affine cuts produce all rows.

There is also an actual endpoint-cover constraint. Put
D=sum_i theta_i alpha_i. If D>0, the B traces cover its whole continuous
space; if D<0 the A traces do; if D=0 both do. For example the weighted
sum of signed cut values at (1,x) is D, so if D>=0 at least one cut
contains (1,x). Therefore the covered endpoint's ordinary centroid
belongs to at least one corresponding cap, giving respectively

    some V_i>=Gamma b, or some U_i>=Gamma a.            (11)

This is shared cap geometry, not merely an independent volume row.

## 4. Exact necessary inequalities under a hypothetical OC failure

If all mixed points failed OC, then in particular

    Gamma<=Q<Gamma m/2.                                (12)

The first inequality follows from the middle centroid, not from an
assumption that y is that centroid. Global endpoint own-depth bounds
also have to remain below the target. If a global maximum D_* is used,
then D_*>=Gamma max(1,a,b) and Q<=D_*<Gamma m/2; one must not silently
replace Q by D_* when the deepest point lies on an endpoint fiber.

At least one critical middle trace contains the ordinary centroid of K.
For every critical cap with q_i>=Gamma, (6) and (12) imply

    T_i:=(U_i+V_i)/q_i < Gamma m/(2q_i)-1
                              <=(a+b-1)/2.             (13)

The noheavy whole-volume theorem
`candidate b572b8df7e9b0f1c`
defines B_d by B_d^d-(2-B_d)^d=1 and y_d=(2-B_d)^d, and proves

    m<=2(1+y_d)<1+sqrt(5).

Thus T_i<y_d. Power concavity also gives

    [U_i^(1/d)+V_i^(1/d)]/[2q_i^(1/d)]
        <=(T_i/2)^(1/d)
        <[(a+b-1)/4]^(1/d)
        <=(y_d/2)^(1/d).                              (14)

Accordingly each such cap must have a LARGE root deficit:

    eta_i:=1-[U_i^(1/d)+V_i^(1/d)]/[2q_i^(1/d)]
       >1-[(a+b-1)/4]^(1/d)
       >=1-(2-B_d)/2^(1/d).                            (15)

The exact noheavy near-BM theorem rules out eta_i at or below the final
threshold, and its simpler condition eta_i<=1/(d+1) gives a uniform
strict OC margin. Equation (15) is the correct direction of inference:
below-target critical caps must be far from captured BM equality. The
volume and cap-budget upper bounds do not force them near equality.

Combining (8) with the centroid conclusion for the covered endpoint in
(11) gives Q>=3Gamma a/2 or Q>=3Gamma b/2, respectively. In particular,
under (12), an endpoint of volume greater than m/3 cannot be the covered
endpoint of this projected critical circuit. This restricts the sign
of its integer drift; it does not bound every individual tilt or force
captured BM equality.

## 5. A rational volume triple beyond these volume-only tests

**Subsequent update.** The joint actual critical-cap profiles plus the
residual-root bound now exclude a below-OC middle maximum for EVERY
compatible planar shape triple with these exact volume ratios; see
`candidate 4dfc7dda63b85569`.
The discussion below remains an exact record of which earlier separate
volume tests and individual cap-row tests failed to settle this tuple.
Its formal row is still valid algebraically, but cannot extend to an
actual below-target critical cover.

Take d=2 and

    (a,1,b)=(1/4,1,121/100), m=123/50, Gamma=4/9.

It satisfies strict noheavy:

    b=121/100<123/100=m/2,
    1<m/2, a<m/2.

Its endpoint roots are 1/2 and 11/10, so R=16/25 and

    R+a=89/100 <123/100=m/2.

Also a=1/4>rho_2 by convention (1). Thus neither the stated heavy,
small-endpoint, equal-endpoint, nor midpoint-centroid volume test settles
all bodies with these volumes.

Even the individual necessary below-target cap inequalities admit exact
rational data. For illustration only, set

    q=4/9, U=1/10, V=1/1800,
    Q=109/200, U+V=181/1800.

Then

    Gamma b=121/225<Q<41/75=Gamma m/2,
    U+V<a, Q<3q,
    (U+V)/q=181/800<23/100=(a+b-1)/2.

Both captured volumes are less than q, so their captured-root BM
inequality is strict. Both strict residual volumes are positive, and
(10) also holds strictly. Indeed their values are 3/20 and 2177/1800;
after one squaring, the residual-root inequality reduces to

    2sqrt((3/20)(2177/1800)) < 1553/1800.

Both sides are positive. The difference of the right side squared and
the left side squared is exactly

    60649/3240000>0.

These numbers are NOT claimed to form an actual critical cap or a
compatible finite critical cover. They only show that the listed scalar
row constraints do not produce an arithmetic contradiction. A global
geometric compatibility argument would still be required.

## 6. Exact actual realization, including genuine far-from-BM critical caps

The volume triple itself is realized by genuine convex-compatible
bodies. Let T be any centroid-zero triangle of area one and set

    A=(1/2)T, K=T, B=(11/10)T.

Then (A+B)/2=(4/5)T subset int T. Their lifted convex hull has exactly
the three desired integer fibers and is a full-dimensional convex body.

This actual example has a complete critical-cap calculation, distinct
from the merely formal data in Section 5. A centroid-zero triangle
satisfies -T subset 2T, as can be checked at its three vertices using
barycentric coordinates. Hence -A subset T subset B. For every ambient
through-(0,0) halfspace, pairing (-1,x), x in A, with (1,-x) in B
shows that the two endpoint captures together have area at least |A|=1/4.
The middle centroid supplies at least 4/9. Thus raw depth there is at
least

    Q_actual=25/36.

For each of the three canonical simplex centroid normals ell_i, the
ambient cap ell_i(x)-Lz>=0 with sufficiently large finite L captures
all of A, misses B, and captures 4/9 of K. These three caps cover K.
They therefore attain Q_actual and bound every middle point's depth
above by Q_actual. Endpoint simplex maximum own depths are 1/9 and
121/225, both smaller than Q_actual, and can be isolated by finite
tilts because the endpoints are exposed. Consequently Q_actual is the
exact global raw maximum.

Each of these genuine critical centroid-cover caps has

    (U,q,V)=(1/4,4/9,0),
    eta=1-(1/2)/(2*(2/3))=5/8>1/3.

Thus even an actual strict-noheavy triple with a complete critical cover
can have its relevant caps far outside the near-BM sufficient regime.
Its true normalized depth is

    Q_actual/m=625/2214>2/9.

It is therefore NOT an OC counterexample. In particular, the formal
Q in Section 5 must not be substituted for its actual Q_actual.

## 7. Coverage conclusion and subsequent closure of the exhibited tuple

The proved small-endpoint and near-BM statements are complementary
sufficient regimes, but they do not constitute a volume-only partition
of all strict-noheavy triples. The first supplies an unspecified small
ratio neighborhood; the second requires actual cap-root data. The earlier
individual row tests in Section 5 left an arithmetic gap at the exhibited
volume triple. That particular gap has now been closed geometrically:
`candidate 4dfc7dda63b85569`
proves a middle point of depth strictly above the OC target for EVERY
compatible planar shape triple with ratios (1/4,1,121/100), by coupling
both actual cap-cover profiles with the residual-root bound.

Thus the formal single row in Section 5 remains arithmetically valid but
cannot extend to an actual below-target critical cover at those ratios.
The explicit triangular realization in Section 6 also remains valid;
it already had depth well above the target. Neither should be recorded
as an unresolved actual volume regime.

A different exact formal three-cap menu at ratios (1/10,1,1) is recorded
in `candidate 45efe8c28e25e4c7`.
It passes the joint scalar profile and residual-volume tests but is NOT
asserted to arise from an actual convex triple or genuinely critical
caps. Its all-zero B captures would require the shared supporting-facet
geometry and full normal-variation inequalities proved in the separate
facet source. That general geometry remains additional to the scalar tests.

The arithmetic and explicit triangular realization in this note are
independently checked in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_three_fiber_regime_remaining_scalar_certificate.py` using exact
rational numbers only. The new volume-tuple closure and the distinct
remaining formal menu are checked in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_joint_profile_planar_volume_exclusion.py`. All files explicitly
keep formal below-target rows separate from actual bodies and depths.
